scheduling.skillGoal: Mechanically enumerate every branching path and boundary in the provided content and report only unhandled edge cases as a structured JSON array
scheduling.intentSignature: Mechanically enumerate paths and boundaries to find unhandled edge cases
intentSignatures: Mechanically enumerate paths and boundaries to find unhandled edge cases
Walk every branching path and boundary condition and report only unhandled cases
Run an exhaustive method-driven edge-case review of code, specs, or diffs
Identify missing handling without commenting on code quality
triggerPatterns: you need exhaustive edge-case analysis of code, specs, or diffs
method-driven (not attitude-driven) edge-case review is requested
diff or function review focused on missing guards

ioContract.inputsRaw: content — Content to review: diff, full file, or function. also_consider (optional) — Areas to keep in mind during review alongside normal edge-case analysis
ioContract.outputsRaw: JSON array of objects, each with exactly: location (file:start-end | file:line | file:hunk), trigger_condition (≤15 words), guard_snippet (single-line escaped string), potential_consequence (≤15 words). Empty array `[]` is valid. On undecodable input, return the documented halt-condition object.

preconditions: content input is provided and decodable as text
scope rules apply (diff → only diff hunks; full file/function → entire content)
external functions are ignored unless explicitly referenced by content

structural.sceneGoal: Receive content, decode it, identify content type, and apply scope rules
Walk every branching path and boundary condition in scope and collect only unhandled paths
Revisit edge classes to confirm no unhandled paths were missed and prune confirmed-handled findings
Emit findings as a JSON array following the strict output format

logical.description: Load the content to review strictly from the provided input
If content is empty or cannot be decoded as text, emit the documented halt-condition JSON and stop
Identify content type (diff, full file, or function) to determine scope rules
If also_consider was provided, incorporate those areas into the analysis alongside normal edge-case classes
Walk all branching paths — control flow (conditionals, loops, error handlers, early returns) and domain boundaries — deriving relevant edge classes from the content itself
For each path, determine whether the content handles it; collect only unhandled paths and discard handled ones silently

Revisit every edge class (missing else/default, null/empty inputs, off-by-one loops, arithmetic overflow, implicit type coercion, race conditions, timeout gaps) to add missed unhandled paths and prune confirmed-handled ones

Output the findings as a strict JSON array of objects with exactly four fields (location, trigger_condition, guard_snippet, potential_consequence) — no extra text, no markdown wrapping; empty array when no unhandled paths found
